accent-strong.note: Accent-strong — the interactive accent (links, active tab, sort chevrons, sliders, progress, selection controls): apple.com's link blue. `--accent` below stays the quiet hover SURFACE; the two are different jobs.

background.note: ═══ Apple palette — light ═══ Minimal and white, after Apple's Human Interface Guidelines and apple.com: a #F5F5F7 page ground under white surfaces (the grouped-list pattern of System Settings and iCloud), near-black #1D1D1F ink with #6E6E73 as the secondary label, hairlines from the system gray ramp, and Apple blue as the one saturated colour. Fills are neutral greys, never tinted. The ground/surface ladder keeps a visible step at every rung, because a hovered white card must never land on the page colour: surface #FFFFFF -> background #F5F5F7 -> muted #EDEDF0 -> strong #E3E3E8

brand-sky.note: Operis brand ramp — theme-invariant (no .dark override). The brand moment (sky → lilac → violet) stays the product's identity; the UI chrome around it follows the Apple palette below.

focus-ring-inner.note: Focus ring halo — Apple blue at low alpha.

font-body.note: Third-party components that theme themselves through their own custom properties rather than inheriting. MDXEditor's stylesheet sets `font-family: var(--font-body)` / `var(--font-mono)` on its editing surface and defines neither, so without these two lines its rich-text area is the one input in the product whose typeface depends on undefined-variable fallback behaviour. Binding them to the product faces makes it explicit. Theme-invariant, like the two faces they alias: a typeface does not change between light and dark.

font-geist-mono.light: "DM Mono", ui-monospace, "SFMono-Regular", "SF Mono", Consolas, "Liberation Mono", Menlo, monospace

font-geist-sans.light: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "SF Pro Display", "SF Pro Text", "Helvetica Neue", "Inter", Arial, sans-serif
font-geist-sans.note: Apple's SF Pro FIRST, then Inter. `-apple-system` / `BlinkMacSystemFont` are Apple-only CSS keywords: on macOS, iOS and iPadOS they resolve to the real SF Pro already installed on the OS — including its automatic SF Pro Text / SF Pro Display optical switching — and on every other platform they match nothing and fall straight through. SF Pro is NOT self-hosted and must not be: Apple's font license covers designing and developing software for Apple platforms, not redistributing the files as a webfont to arbitrary browsers. Inter therefore stays as the self-hosted face every non-Apple client gets; it is the closest open equivalent to SF and keeps Windows/Linux from falling back to Segoe UI or Cantarell. Inter / DM Mono are self-hosted (see ./fonts.css) because the app's CSP is `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` with no external hosts, so a Google Fonts <link> is blocked at runtime. "SF Pro Display" / "SF Pro Text" / "Helvetica Neue" name locally installed faces only — nothing is downloaded — and Arial is the last resort if Inter ever fails to load.

font-size-overline.note: ═══ Design System: Typography ═══ The scale is deliberately narrow. A page title is LIGHT (400) and large; weight is spent on the things that must be scanned — table headers, tabs, nav items — not on the heading, which already has size.

input-bg.note: Input family — fields are filled wells, not white boxes: the same control fill as the soft button, so a form reads as one material and needs no border.

primary.note: Apple blue. The system blue #007AFF carries white text at only 4.0:1, so fills use apple.com's button blue, which clears AA (4.7:1).

primary-soft.note: The soft button and the field well are one material: Apple's control fill.

radius-sm.note: ═══ Design System: Radius Scale ═══ Explicit values rather than offsets from a single `--radius`, so each step is a decision instead of a side effect: sm = inline chips and checkboxes, md = compact buttons and menu items, lg = default controls (button, input, nav item), xl = cards, tables and popovers, 2xl = modals and sheets. The steps are concentric: a menu row (md) inside a menu's 6px padding lands exactly on the menu's own corner (xl).

shadow-elevation-xs.note: Elevation values behind the `shadow-*` scale (see the Shadow Scale note in `@theme`). The floating steps open with a 0.5px edge in place of a border.

shadow-focus.note: Focus indicator — ONE mechanism for the whole product. The design reference suppresses focus rings entirely; we keep them (a keyboard user must be able to see where they are) but adopt the intent: quiet. A 2px ground-coloured inner ring separates the halo from the control, then a 4px blue halo at low alpha. Because it is a token, the whole app's focus treatment moves as one decision.

shadow-switch-thumb.note: Switch thumb: thin drop shadow + hairline outline (matches Figma switch spec).

shadow-xs.note: ═══ Design System: Shadow Scale ═══ Apple-style elevation: neutral black at low alpha with a wide, soft blur, so a raised surface floats rather than carrying a hard edge. xs → flat controls (button, input, icon-button) sm → cards, table cards, panels md → hover lift, the floating search field, toasts lg → menus, popovers, dropdowns xl → floating panels (drawers, side sheets) 2xl → top-level modals, command palette The floating levels (lg and up) open with a 0.5px edge, the hairline a menu shows on macOS, so a surface needs no border to hold its shape on a white page. Each step points at a `--shadow-elevation-*` value defined per theme in `:root` / `.dark`. `@theme inline` bakes a literal value into the utility, so a shadow written here directly could never change with the theme.

sidebar.note: Sidebar family — the product's INKED chrome: the selected capsule of the default segmented control, the chrome tone of the search field and the live preview in the sidebar customization editor. Apple paints a selected capsule near-black with light ink (apple.com's filter and product chips), so the family is a complete dark set — ink, quiet ink, hover fill, active pill, hairline — rather than borrowing the light content-side neutrals.

status-pink-bg.note: Pink — a CATEGORICAL accent for stage/category chips, never a semantic outcome. System pink.

table-header.note: Table family — a list view is the most-used surface in the product, so its parts are named instead of expressed as opacity math at call sites. The header shares the card's white, as in Finder's list view: the column labels carry it, with one hairline under the header strip.

text-large-title.note: ═══ Design System: Type Scale ═══ Tailwind's scale covers every step of the hierarchy except the page title, which sits between `text-3xl` (30px) and `text-4xl` (36px). One token for it, used by `PageHeader`, so every page title lands on the same size.
